Programme Preamble
types.description: Opening orientation for the programme prose: what the prose is, the line between description and procedure, the six areas of the corpus and the style of the prose.

types.label: Mission
types.description: The programme's originating mission — why the research began, the theological conviction that shaped its scope, and the two Framework documents it produced.

types.label: Scope
types.description: The scope of the study: the ESV surfaces of the groups behaviour and inner_being_state, each in one collection, and how scope is settled and changed.

types.label: This Inner-Being Programme
types.description: What the programme is: its unit of study and of reading, its working agent and the researcher's authority, the application that controls it and its three levels of output.

types.label: Defining Inner Being
types.description: The programme's working definition of inner-being characteristics — verbatim, with the three boundary decisions embedded in it, the spirit/soul distinction it holds open, and the inclusion rule that governs its application.

types.label: Science and the Bible
types.description: The programme's two-lens architecture — Scripture as primary lens, science as second lens — what each provides and cannot provide, the convergence and divergence framework, and the governing principles of their interaction.

types.label: Expected Outcome
types.description: What success looks like for a collection, for the corpus and for the programme, the intended audience and the three criteria by which the finished output is judged.

types.label: Research method
types.description: The research method at a glance: its five parts from the text and its data to publishing, the collection as the unit of study, and the lens and sequencing commitments.

types.label: Word selection: surfaces and collections
types.description: How scope is built: the four surface groups, the surface cycle, the collections, and the caveats on each.

types.label: Programme flow
types.description: The path from the Bible text to the finished account: the base data; the stages of the analysis with the unit each reads; the subgroup and its purpose; volume, gates and fallout; the inner-being layer; where the programme stands; what is unsolved and what is not yet defined.

types.label: Science in action
types.description: How the second lens is engaged: when science enters (in the claims reading), the six fields, the convergence and divergence framework and the decision not to build a scientific database.

types.label: Publishing
types.description: The output of the programme: the narrative held in the database as chapters and sections, how claims are told in it, and what publishing does and does not mean here.

types.label: Key methodological principles
types.description: The principles that govern every stage, the lessons of the programme's course from which they come, the difficulty not yet resolved and the researcher's test.

types.label: Key constraints
types.description: The limits the programme accepts as commitments: scope bounded by the collections, the second-lens bound on science, no scientific database, no bulk analysis and no publication before the reading closes.

types.label: Traceability and evidential warrant
types.description: The discipline that separates a finding from a hypothesis and an inferential statement: traceability to the data, the verse as the evidence, the database as the authority and verified state.

types.label: The two-AI division of responsibility
types.description: The division of responsibility between the researcher and the single working agent, the controlled use of a local model, and the two mechanisms that carry the researcher's decisions.

types.label: Session continuity and memory discipline
types.description: How continuity is kept across sessions: the databases as memory, the layers and limits of Claude's memory, and the mechanisms for starting, recording and closing a session.

types.label: Tools and their roles
types.description: The programme's instruments and their roles: STEP Bible, Claude Code, the IBA application, the two databases, the local model server and the working file formats.

types.label: Researcher decision authority
types.description: The researcher's authority and accountability, Claude's expected interpretation of the evidence, the integrity of the sources and the declaration of AI use.

types.label: Scope and help-forward discipline
types.description: The in-session discipline that keeps Claude on the task set: help forward within the researcher's scope, no autonomous extension of scope, and escalation and not guessing.

types.label: The database as the programme's working memory
types.description: The two databases as the programme's working memory: what each holds, the configuration store and STEP Bible as the primary source.

sections_preview.heading: The database as the programme's working memory
sections_preview.author: claude_code

types.label: Surfaces, collections and the registry
types.description: Where scope is held: the surface and collection tables, the subgroup tables, and the thin registry that onboards a new word.

types.label: Terms
types.description: The term layer: the Strong's tables, the span and the mechanical reading of the verse, with the key each is held on.

types.label: Ownership and cross-registry references
types.description: How overlap of vocabulary is handled: each surface in one collection, the collection a node carries, and the keying of the term layer on the Strong's code.

types.label: Verses and the context layer
types.description: The verse layer: the verse table, when a verse is in scope, and how every observation is tied to its verse.

types.label: The node
types.description: The node: how one observation is applied to a verse, a word and a surface, its roles, and the rules that keep nodes and observations consistent.

types.label: The analytical grouping: collections and subgroups
types.description: The analytical grouping: the collection, the subgroup, the observation tables and the ledger of the layered reading.

sections_preview.author: claude_code

types.label: The question catalogue and findings
types.description: The standing catalogue of questions as prompts, the findings of the programme as observations, and the kept record of earlier methods.

types.label: Claims and the narrative
types.description: Claims and the narrative: the claim tables, the narrative chapters and sections, and how claims are bound to the observations that found them.

types.label: The prose store
types.description: The prose store: the section types, the sections and the glossaries, the system-versioned lifecycle, and the steps of Prose.ps1.

types.label: Capture mechanisms
types.description: The capture mechanisms: prose through the Prose.ps1 round trip, observations through the layered reading, and open items through the escalation table.

types.label: Document validation and quality-flag architecture
types.description: The standing checks that tell a session whether the application, the record and the study are coherent, and the quality flags of the prose store.

types.label: Soft-delete discipline
types.description: The soft-delete discipline across both databases, its table-level form, and the rule against hard deletes.

types.label: Record consistency with sources
types.description: How the record stays consistent with its sources: field authority, observation-reference consistency and STEP data provenance.

types.label: Backup and schema migration discipline
types.description: Backup and schema migration discipline for each database, and the named snapshots kept before a change to the collections or the observations.

types.label: Patch and directive failure protocol
types.description: The failure protocol: dry-run rejection of patches, routing of failures by cfg_on_fail in the application, and escalation of what cannot be resolved mechanically.

types.label: Instruction override and cross-document reference discipline
types.description: How the researcher's direction travels: configuration changes by proposal and approval, the escalation table for everything else, and where the rules live.

types.label: Documentation–implementation alignment
types.description: The principle that rules, schema, documents and prose are not assumed to be synchronised, and the rules that keep them aligned.

types.label: Global rules
types.description: Where the programme's binding rules live: configuration rows, printed at the start of a session or delivered at first use.

types.label: Reference
types.description: The live reference layer: the enumerations, the column definitions and the configuration report that other documents point to.

types.label: Patches
types.description: The patch mechanism of bible_research.db: its format, the PROSE operation and the dry-run gate.

types.label: Directives
types.description: The directive mechanism of bible_research.db, and how a schema change reaches iba.db.

types.label: Claude Code operating guide
types.description: Where the operating guidance for Claude Code lives: the start and close routines, the point-of-use rules and the application documents.

types.label: Registry management guide
types.description: The registry management guide: none is held, and why.

types.label: Base data
types.description: How the base data is built: the entry point for a new word and the mechanical reading of the verse.

types.label: The collection reading
types.description: How a collection is read through the layered reading: the routines, the order of the steps and the ledger.

types.label: The grouping of the surfaces
types.description: How the surfaces of a collection are grouped: the grouping routines, the status of the method, and how a collection is changed.

types.label: Readiness of a step
types.description: How a step of the reading is made ready: opening it, pulling its rows and the working file.

types.label: Recording observations
types.description: How the reading's output is recorded and checked: the record step, the layer check and the other capture mechanisms.

types.label: The narrative
types.description: The reader-facing output: the narrative built by collection, its export, and the claims told in it.

types.description: Synthesis across collections and the claims: what is established, and what is deferred and not built.
